claims.text: DFT-based ab initio molecular dynamics can accurately predict low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The predictive approach works by modeling phonon-phonon interactions.
The approach applies to high-entropy alloys in as-cast or annealed states.
The intended operating-temperature range is 300–1000 K.
Lattice dynamics and phonon dispersion relations are the structural mediators connecting the simulation approach to thermal-conductivity prediction.
First-principles DFT calculations accurately capture anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions in high-entropy alloys.
Capturing anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions improves predictions of phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach will predict phonon thermal conductivities that are 10–20% lower than current predictions.
The approach will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than current methods.
Current predictions are based on empirical or semi-empirical models.
The approach is limited to high-entropy alloys with known crystal structures and compositions.
The approach may not apply to alloys with complex or unknown structures.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the selected exchange-correlation functional.
Prediction accuracy may be affected by the available computational resources.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing simulated and experimentally measured phonon thermal conductivities for a set of high-entropy alloys.
A prediction error greater than 30% relative to experiment constitutes falsification.
